record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: For house allocation via exchanges in a social network, which exchange mechanisms are strategyproof, and under what structural restrictions on the network or exchange rules can strategyproofness be achieved?

evidence.quote: Strategyproofness is another topic worthy of investigation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following model of house allocation via exchanges on a social network. Let G = (N, E) be an undirected graph whose vertex set N = {1, ..., n} represents agents and whose edge set E encodes a social network (an edge {i, j} ∈ E means agents i and j are acquaintances). Each agent i ∈ N initially owns one indivisible house h_i, and has a strict preference order ≻_i over the set of houses {h_1, ..., h_n}. An exchange mechanism is a function f that takes as input the reported preference profile (≻_i)_{i ∈ N} (and possibly the network G) and outputs an allocation π : N → {h_1, ..., h_n} that is a permutation of the initial endowment, subject to the constraint that exchanges respect the network structure (for example, only agents connected by an edge, or lying in a common connected subset, may trade houses, or trading cycles must be subgraphs of G).

A mechanism f is strategyproof if for every agent i, every preference profile (≻_j)_{j ∈ N}, and every alternative report ≻'_i, the house assigned to i under truthful reporting is weakly preferred (under the true ≻_i) to the house assigned to i when i reports ≻'_i.

Problem. Characterize the exchange mechanisms on social networks that are strategyproof. In particular:
(a) Identify structural restrictions on the network G (e.g., trees, bounded degree, bipartite, complete) under which there exist nontrivial strategyproof exchange mechanisms satisfying additional desiderata such as individual rationality, Pareto efficiency (with respect to feasible exchanges), and non-wastefulness.
(b) Identify restrictions on the allowed exchange rules (e.g., bounded cycle length, only pairwise swaps, only swaps along edges, top trading cycles restricted to the network) under which strategyproofness can be guaranteed.
(c) Provide impossibility results delineating the boundary between settings admitting strategyproof exchange mechanisms and those in which strategyproofness is incompatible with the chosen efficiency/fairness criteria.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has made partial progress on this question. In particular, an AAMAS 2022 paper "Strategy-Proof House Allocation with Existing Tenants over Social Networks" proposes a modified YRMH-IGYT mechanism that is individually rational, strategy-proof, and weakly non-wasteful, and proves impossibility results (e.g., even on tree-structured networks, no strategy-proof and individually rational mechanism is non-wasteful). Further work on online housing markets and on strategy-proofness in network auctions continues to explore the boundary. A complete characterization of strategyproof network-exchange mechanisms remains open.

status_evidence.title: Strategy-Proof House Allocation with Existing Tenants over Social Networks
status_evidence.snippet: A modified YRMH-IGYT mechanism is individually rational, strategy-proof, weakly non-wasteful; impossibility on tree networks for stronger welfare.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive and negative results have been obtained for strategyproof exchange/allocation in network settings.

status_evidence.title: Online Housing Market
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to study strategy-proof exchange mechanisms in network/online settings.
status_evidence.claim: The line of investigation remains active with ongoing partial results.
